To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the binding of an AMPA receptor agonist is accompanied by a conformational change in the agonist binding site, and that the conformational change is induced by the agonist.

(1) the Glu receptor ligand-binding domain is composed of a central ligand-binding core and two peripheral domains, which are connected via two flexible linkers; (2) the agonist-binding site is composed of a binding pocket, formed mainly by residues of the ligand-binding domain, and an adjacent water molecule; and (3) agonist binding induces conformational changes of the ligand binding domain.
the binding of agonist ligands to the agonist binding site is mediated by a combination of hydrophobic, ionic and hydrogen-bonding interactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural basis for ligand-receptor interactions in iGluRs, and we have used the AMPA receptor as a prototype to study the molecular basis for ligand selectivity and receptor activation.
the structural and functional characterization of iGluR subtypes, and with the development of novel ligands for these receptors.

the development of novel ligands that can be used as pharmacological probes to study the role of AMPA receptors in normal and pathologic brain function and as lead compounds for the development of new drugs to treat neurodegenerative disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the agonist binding site of AMPA receptors, there are no significant differences between the crystal structures of the apo form and the agonist-bound form.
the agonists of AMPA receptor subtypes are able to bind in two distinct binding modes, the open and the closed mode.
the binding domain of iGluR subunits is an allosteric receptor with a binding pocket that can accommodate a number of different ligands.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have provided the structural basis for the design of AMPA receptor ligands, which is a prerequisite for the development of drugs for the treatment of brain diseases.
we have been able to show the molecular basis for the binding of agonists to AMPA receptors.
we now have a structural basis for rational drug design for AMPA receptor subtype selective agonists, antagonists and allosteric modulators.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding pocket of the agonist is very well conserved in all iGluR subtypes, but the binding mode is not.
the Glu receptor agonist binding site is highly conserved among all Glu receptor subtypes, which has facilitated the rational design of subtype-selective agonists.
the agonists bind in a similar manner in the two different subtypes of AMPA receptors (GluA2 and GluA4).
